title: Sales anchor cards — decision crumbs (draft)
body:
Purpose
-----
Rapid, pocket-sized reference for sellers and SEs to anchor conversations with platform/prod-engineering buyers. Focus: decisions (not exhaustive specs). One-sheet cards per decision point with 30s opening, 90s technical note, and 1–2 lines of next-step CTA.

Audience
--------
- Platform architects and infra/ML platform leads at mid-market/enterprise
- SEs trying to triage pilot fit in 10–15 mins
- AEs who want a compact way to escalate to solutions engineering

Design constraints / tone
-----------------------
- 30–90 second talking points, quantified where possible (latency, cost delta)
- Honest: call out tradeoffs and conditions for fallback
- Actionable CTA: what to pilot, which logs to capture, who to loop in
- Lightweight visuals only — handed as single-slide printable cards

Card inventory (proposed)
------------------------
1) Latency-first routing decision card
   - 30s opener: "If sub-200ms 99th percentile is table stakes, route to 'low-latency' variants, pin model family X, enable short-seq caching."
   - 90s tech note: continuous batching reduces p99 variance but increases token cost; prefer micro-batching (max batch size 8) + prefix-KV cache for stable prompts.
   - Metrics to call out: p50/p95/p99, token cost per 1k reqs, failover latency to compatible variant.
   - CTA: Run a 1-hour synthetics sweep (50qps, realistic seq dist) and attach perf trace.

2) Cost-constrained recommendation card
   - 30s opener: "If economics are the blocker, show reserved pools + quantized model variants. We can cut per-token spend 2–3x in many cases."
   - 90s tech note: quantization choice affects QA — 8-bit QAT vs 4-bit PTQ tradeoffs; prefer A/B pilot on 5% traffic.
   - Callouts: billing granularity (tokens vs inference units), minimum commit for Dedicated offers.
   - CTA: Propose 2-week AB pilot with billing export + cost dashboard access.

3) Private/vpc compliance card
   - 30s opener: "Regulatory requirement? Private deployment + KMS integration + audit logs. Redwoods private control-plane option available."
   - 90s tech note: on-prem adds ops burden — document ingress/egress requirements, network ACLs, and secret rotation cadence.
   - CTA: Start with architecture review workshop (60–90m), collect compliance checklist items.

4) Fallback and graceful degradation card
   - 30s opener: "Design for graceful fallback: model variants + regional failover + throttled responses."
   - 90s tech note: implement sentinel route that monitors tail-latency and triggers reroute to smaller model variant; include end-to-end tracing.
   - CTA: Add canary rule to rollout config; set the threshold to X ms for auto-fallback.

5) Data residency & PII minimization card
   - 30s opener: "If PII is a blocker, propose token scrub preflight + per-customer KV cache and selective logging."
   - 90s tech note: ingestion-time redaction reduces model quality for some prompts — consider client-side redaction + staged eval.
   - CTA: Collect 10 representative queries and run an offline redaction + quality check.

Quick rebuttal snippets (objection -> quick answer)
--------------------------------------------------
- "We can’t commit to a reserved contract": show short-term Dedicated burst and usage vs commit calculator; offer a 90-day cap.
- "Latency is unpredictable": point to per-token breakdowns in console + model verified perf profiles; propose synthetics with guarded slate.
- "Open models are risky for hallucination": recommend prompt engineering guardrails, eval harness, and reranking layer.
- "We don’t want vendor lock-in": remind unified API + model-variant routing; share migration plan in 4 steps.

Pilot checklist (1-page)
----------------------
- Primary goal defined (latency / cost / GDPR / accuracy)
- 1 owner on customer side + 1 SE lead
- Dataset slices and 50–100 golden prompts
- Traffic profile: qps, seq length distribution, concurrency
- Success metrics: p95 latency target, per-request cost threshold, quality acceptance criteria
- Logging/trace collection enabled, telemetry ingestion point (S3/BigQuery)
- Rollout policy: canary % and auto-fallback thresholds

Slide/handout structure (6 slides/cards max)
-------------------------------------------
- Title + one-liner outcome
- Decision cards (3–4 mini cards per slide)
- Pilot checklist (single slide)
- Next steps & contacts (who to loop in)
- FAQ / quick rebuttals (1 slide)

Open questions / things to validate
--------------------------------
- Standardize the numeric deltas for "cost savings from quantization" — need real perf numbers from Applied ML (ping: PR to capture experiments).
- What is the minimum commit threshold for Dedicated that legal can approve for pilot discounts? (Liam to confirm).
- Which telemetry schema do we require for pilot (trace fields, token-level cost)? Align with observability team.

To-dos (next 2 weeks)
--------------------
- Maya: draft 6 printable cards in Figma (due 2026-02-20)
- Evan: run synthetic perf sweep for the latency card and drop results into linked artifact (GTMP-412) by 2026-02-18
- Priya: schedule 3 seller role plays + capture verbatim objections (2026-02-22)
- Liam: confirm legal floor for short-term reserved pricing by 2026-02-19

Notes to self / messy bits
-------------------------
- Keep each card <150 words.
- Might combine latency + fallback into single card for smaller pack.
- Consider a "single-page cheat sheet" for SEs that includes exact CLI snippets for quick verifications (curl + SDK).
- Draft needs to be consumable offline (pdf print).

References + existing assets
--------------------------
- Related slide pack: platform-onboard-30-60-90-playbook-wip (drive) — use as narrative spine
- Perf traces: GH PR 834 (internal repo)
- Legal pricing notes: finance-and-legal/pilot-credits-templates (drive)

Appendix: example 30s script (latency card)
----------------------------------------
"For teams that require sub-200ms tail latency, we recommend pinning small-model family A on dedicated pool and enabling prefix cache. In our tests with realistic conversational loads, p99 dropped from ~750ms to ~180ms with micro-batch size 4 and a hot-prefix cache. For pilots we provision a 2x burst buffer and collect traces for three days — if you want, I’ll schedule the perf sweep with your infra team tomorrow."

End of draft — flagged for GTM review.

(rough, please add exact numbers + perf artifacts before wider share)
